The support story: around-the-clock coverage claimed, exact figures conflicting.
The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.
The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Fill in the registration form and activate the account via the confirmation email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Complete the US$200 deposit to unlock the live dashboard.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your limits, pick a trading mode and let the demo build your confidence first.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
redFlags: Payout promises with no processing detail.
No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.
Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.

faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.
US$200, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$200 minimum.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$200 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

bottomLine: LeverCat is a standard-issue AI trading desk with the usual strengths and the usual omissions. None of the omissions are dealbreakers - they are conditions.
The verdict holds at 4.6: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
